content:
Apple confirmed that a special product launch event named "Welcome Home" will be held next Tuesday (October 13), but has not yet announced whether a keynote video will be released on the same day. Here is what we know so far.

Apple has yet to confirm whether a "Welcome Home" keynote will take place, but Mark Gurman has revealed there will be an "online video announcement."

Apple has been innovating its traditional product launch approach throughout this year. The MacBook Neo unveiled in March was the first example—after releasing several new products via press releases over consecutive days, a "hands-on experience" event was held to let the media try out the new devices in person.

It looks like Apple's "Welcome Home" event on October 13 will once again innovate in a similar manner.

Unlike previous events, Apple has not yet added "Welcome Home" to the Apple Events webpage, and there are no signs of any livestream on YouTube or the Apple TV app.

Things may still change in the days leading up to the event, but based on the current situation, it seems there will not be a keynote video on October 13.

However, Mark Gurman mentioned in a Bloomberg report that a video announcement will be made. In an article discussing another Apple event scheduled for October 27, he wrote:

According to Gurman—who had previously accurately reported the date of October 13, as well as the fact that the event would focus on home products—Apple will hold an "online video announcement" next week.

The media will attend the "Apple Experience" hands-on event starting at 9 a.m. New York time that day. So if a launch video is released on the day, it will most likely go online around that time, which is quite a bit earlier than the usual keynote broadcast time.

We expect at least three new products to be unveiled on Tuesday—details can be found here.

What do you think—will Apple release a keynote video for "Welcome Home"? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
